name: Warm editorial, titled (wiki hero strips)
styleLine: warm editorial illustration, soft painterly line and gentle shading, muted natural palette on a warm cream ground, grounded and human, picture-book register for adults
rejectedPoles: any identifiable recurring individual's face or signature clothing
gate: warm editorial painterly illustration, soft brushwork; NOT comic, NOT flat vector, NOT photoreal, NOT 3D
muted natural palette on a warm cream ground

no figure carries the likeness the style references leak: nobody wears a denim or jean jacket, a chest patch, a smiley-face badge, an enamel pin or a white tee under an open jacket, and nobody is a recognizable real public figure; any of these is a DEFECT. People are ordinary and drawn from the scene's own description

ONE consistent cast: the person using the glowing laptop is the same person in every panel they appear in, with the same face, hair, age and clothing. That recurrence is the strip's law and is never a DEFECT; a different person in that role from one panel to the next is a DEFECT

whoever is using the glowing laptop is shot from behind them, over their shoulder: they are nearer to the camera than the laptop is, its screen faces them, and we look past them into it. A laptop standing between the camera and the person using it, whichever way its lid faces, is a DEFECT
every declared string is present and spelled character-exact; a near-miss is a DEFECT
no text beyond the declared strings; invented lettering is a DEFECT
the title bar sits across the top margin and each label in its own band at the top of its panel, never lettered over the artwork; there is no footer bar and none is expected
